query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A graph neural network-based model can be used to design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions by predicting the properties of HEAs from their composition data.
generation.material_initial_state: Multi-principal elements with huge selections of composition
generation.intervention: Training a graph neural network-based model on a dataset of HEA compositions and their corresponding properties
generation.mechanism: The graph neural network-based model learns to predict the properties of HEAs by identifying patterns in the composition data and relating them to the atomic interactions and crystal structure
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase of 20% in yield strength and a decrease of 15% in density compared to the baseline RHEA composition
generation.baseline: A conventional RHEA composition with a yield strength of 1000 MPa and a density of 8 g/cm^3
generation.boundary: The model's predictions are valid for HEA compositions with up to 5 principal elements and operating temperatures up to 1000°C
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the model's predictions may be affected by the quality and size of the training dataset, as well as the complexity of the HEA compositions

falsification_experiment.design: Train the graph neural network-based model on a dataset of HEA compositions and their corresponding properties, and then test its predictions on a separate dataset of HEA compositions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the model's predictions are not within 10% of the actual values for at least 80% of the test dataset, the hypothesis is falsified
